([[Seattle]], Washington) | draft_year = 2005 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 6 | draft_team = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | career_start = 2005 | career_end = 2015 | career_number = 8, 23, 5, 9 | career_position = [[Small forward]] / [[shooting guard]] | years1 ={{nbay|2005|start}}–{{nbay|2009|end}} | team1 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | years2 =2006 | team2 = →[[Fort Worth Flyers]] | years3 ={{nbay|2010|start}}–{{nbay|2011|end}} | team3 = [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] | years4 ={{nbay|2012|start}}–{{nbay|2015|start}} | team4 = [[Washington Wizards]] | highlights= *First-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (2005) *[[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2005 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2005]]) | stat1label = [[Point (basketball)|Points]] | stat1value = (8.7 ppg) | stat2label = [[Rebound (basketball)|Rebounds]] | stat2value = (3.1 rpg) | stat3label = [[Assist (basketball)|Assists]] | stat3value = (1.0 apg) }} '''Martell Webster''' (born December 4, 1986) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played ten seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). The sixth player taken in the [[2005 NBA draft]], Webster played for [[Portland Trail Blazers|Portland]], [[Minnesota Timberwolves|Minnesota]] and [[Washington Wizards|Washington]] between 2005 and 2015. His best season came in [[2012–13 Washington Wizards season|2012–13]] when he started 62 games for the Wizards and averaged 11.4 points per game. ==High school career== Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Webster was listed as the No. 4 shooting guard and the No. 5 player in the nation in 2005.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Martell-Webster-21634;_ylt=Apify7Ggu8wIgqiwegTtM25GPZB4|title=Martell Webster Recruiting Profile|publisher=Rivals.com|access-date=February 28, 2012}} He had made a commitment to the [[University of Washington]], but opted to go [[prep-to-pro]]. ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers (2005–2010)=== Webster was selected by the Blazers with the sixth pick in the [[2005 NBA draft]] after the Blazers' traded their third pick to the [[Utah Jazz]] just hours before the draft.{{cite web|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/draft/2005-06-28-blazers-jazz-trade_x.htm|title=Jazz get No. 3 overall pick from Blazers in trade|publisher=USAToday.com|date=June 28, 2005|access-date=February 28, 2012}} He was assigned to the [[Fort Worth Flyers]] of the [[NBA Development League]] by the Blazers in January 2006, and in doing so became highest-drafted player (6th overall) to be assigned to the D-League until [[Hasheem Thabeet]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/affiliates_review_0708.html|title=NBA Affiliates In Review|work=NBA.com|date=August 13, 2007|access-date=February 28, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121104053716/http://www.nba.com/dleague/affiliates_review_0708.html|archive-date=November 4, 2012|df=mdy-all}} He later returned to the Portland Trail Blazers in February 2006. He scored a season-high 26 points in a January 5, 2008, win over the [[Utah Jazz]], with 24 of them scored in the third quarter.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280105022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809061959/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280105022|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 9, 2020|title=Webster scores 24 third-quarter points in Blazers' blowout|work=ESPN.com |date=January 5, 2008|access-date=October 6, 2020}} He is one of the last-ever [[high school]] players to be chosen in an [[NBA draft]] due to new draft eligibility rules introduced in 2006. In October 2008, Webster signed a four-year, $20 million contract extension.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3675835|title=Agent: Trail Blazers sign swingman Webster to 4-year extension|work=ESPN.com |date=October 31, 2008|access-date=October 6, 2020}} On February 20, 2009, it was announced by Trail Blazers athletic trainer Jay Jensen that Webster would likely miss the rest of the [[2008–09 NBA season]] with a left foot injury, having only played 5 minutes during the season.{{cite web |title=Blazers' Martell Webster likely out for rest of regular season |date=February 20, 2009 |publisher=[[OregonLive.com]] |access-date=February 21, 2009 |first=Jason |last=Quick |url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/behindblazersbeat/2009/02/breaking_news_webster_likely_o.html}} On January 23, 2010, he scored a season-high 28 points in a win against the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web |title=Blazers' Portland 97, Detroit 93: Blazers Keep Defying the Odds |date=January 23, 2010 |publisher=[[OregonLive.com]] |access-date=January 23, 2010 |first=Jason |last=Quick |url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/behindblazersbeat/2010/01/portland_97_detroit_93_webster.html}}{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=300123008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171002120323/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=300123008|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 2, 2017|title=Blazers stop Pistons despite having only eight players|date=January 23, 2010|access-date=October 6, 2020|agency=Associated Press}} ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2010–2012)=== Webster was traded on June 24, 2010, to the Minnesota Timberwolves in exchange for [[Ryan Gomes]] and the rights to draft pick [[Luke Babbitt]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2010/news/story?id=5325319|title=2010 NBA draft: Washington Wizards select John Wall at No. 1 - ESPN|work=ESPN.com |date=June 25, 2010|access-date=October 6, 2020}} Webster underwent back surgery in October 2010 and missed nearly half the 2010–11 NBA season, leading Timberwolves general manager [[David Kahn (sports executive)|David Kahn]] to charge the Trail Blazers with failure to adequately disclose a known injury.{{cite web|first=Henry|last=Abbott|title=The resolution of the Martell Webster dispute|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/truehoop/post/_/id/57679|access-date=October 6, 2020|work=ESPN.com|date=May 3, 2013}} Another back surgery followed in September 2011, limiting Webster to just 47 games for the Wolves in the 2011–12 season.{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Golliver|title=Abbott: Blazers Paid Off Timberwolves In Dispute Over Martell Webster|url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2013/5/3/4298228/abbott-blazers-paid-off-timberwolves-in-dispute-over-martell-webster|access-date=October 6, 2020|work=BlazersEdge.com|date=May 3, 2013}} In spring 2013 Kahn's complaint was reportedly settled by the Blazers for $1.5 million just before the matter was brought to a formal hearing before the NBA. It was said to be among the largest cash settlements in such a case. Both teams were sworn to secrecy about the exact terms of the deal, according to basketball journalist Henry Abbott of [[ESPN]]. On July 13, 2012, Webster was waived by the Timberwolves.{{cite news|title=Timberwolves waive Martell Webster|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8164708|access-date=October 6, 2020|work=ESPN.com|date=July 13, 2012}} ===Washington Wizards (2012–2015)=== [[File:Martell Webster shooting.jpg|thumb|Webster shooting a jumpshot over [[Evan Turner]], 2013]] Webster signed with the [[Washington Wizards]] on August 29, 2012, on a one-year, $1.6 million contract.{{cite news|title=Washington Wizards sign Martell Webster|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10835|access-date=August 29, 2012|work=InsideHoops.com|date=August 29, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130206101034/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10835|archive-date=February 6, 2013|url-status=dead}} On March 16, 2013, Webster scored a career-high 34 points in a win over the [[Phoenix Suns]], also tying another career high with seven three-pointers. On July 10, 2013, Webster re-signed with the Wizards.{{cite news|title=Wizards Re-Sign Martell Webster|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-re-sign-martell-webster|access-date=July 10, 2013|work=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2013}} In [[2014–15 Washington Wizards season|2014–15]], Webster missed the first 30 games of the season after he underwent surgery in June 2014 to repair a herniated disk in his lower back. He was ruled out for three to five months,{{cite news|first=Jake|last=Whitacre|title=Martell Webster to miss 3-5 months after back surgery|url=http://www.bulletsforever.com/2014/6/27/5850142/martell-webster-herniated-disc-surgery-washington-wizards|access-date=June 27, 2014|work=BulletsForever.com|date=June 27, 2014}} as he returned to action on December 30, 2014, against the Dallas Mavericks.{{cite web|title=Martell Webster 2014-15 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/webstma02/gamelog/2015/|access-date=November 20, 2015|work=Basketball-Reference.com}} On November 20, 2015, Webster was ruled out for the 2015–16 season after undergoing successful surgery to repair the labrum and damaged cartilage in his right hip.{{cite news|title=WEBSTER UNDERGOES HIP PROCEDURE|url=http://wizardstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/11/20/webster-undergoes-hip-procedure|access-date=November 20, 2015|work=WizardsToday.MonumentalNetwork.com|date=November 20, 2015}} He was subsequently waived by the Wizards ten days later.{{cite news|title=WIZARDS WAIVE WEBSTER, SIGN HOLLINS|url=http://wizardstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/11/30/wizards-waive-webster-sign-hollins|access-date=November 30, 2015|work=WizardsToday.MonumentalNetwork.com|date=November 30, 2015|archive-date=November 30, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151130200732/http://wizardstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/11/30/wizards-waive-webster-sign-hollins|url-status=dead}} ===Retirement=== On September 25, 2017, Webster was added to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]' training camp roster.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-announce-2017-training-camp-roster|title=Pelicans Announce 2017 Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=September 25, 2017|access-date=September 25, 2017}} However, five days later, he decided to leave training camp and retire from basketball.{{cite web|last=Kosel|first=Oleh|url=https://www.thebirdwrites.com/2017/9/30/16390786/martell-webster-twitter-retirement-new-orleans-pelicans-wizards-trail-blazers|title=Martell Webster cuts NBA comeback attempt short, announces retirement on social media|work=thebirdwrites.com|date=September 30, 2017|access-date=September 30, 2017|archive-date=January 26, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220126082654/https://www.thebirdwrites.com/2017/9/30/16390786/martell-webster-twitter-retirement-new-orleans-pelicans-wizards-trail-blazers|url-status=dead}} McGuirk, disappeared in 1990, when he was four years old. Although her body was never found, [[Gary Ridgway]], known as the "Green River Killer", a serial killer who murdered dozens of women and girls in Washington during the 1980s and 1990s, is thought to be responsible for killing her.{{Cite news|last=Kogod|first=Sarah|date=2013-04-15|title=Martell Webster on learning to be a family man and team player|language=en-US|newspaper=[[Washington Post]]|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/dc-sports-bog/wp/2013/04/15/martell-webster-on-learning-to-be-a-family-man-and-team-player/|access-date=2022-02-07|issn=0190-8286}} His cousin is former NBA veteran [[Jason Terry]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/truehoop/post/_/id/190|title=Blazers Present Martell Webster|work=ESPN.com|date=June 29, 2005|access-date=December 8, 2025}} In 2015, Webster co-founded [[EYRST]], an [[independent record label]] focusing on [[Hip hop music|hip hop]], based in [[Portland, Oregon]]. He released his first [[mixtape]], ''ARTT'', on July 14, 2016,{{cite web|url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2016/7/14/12104946/nba-player-portland-trail-blazers-martell-webster-artt-is-honest-quality-hip-hop-eyrst-music|title=Martell Webster's ARTT is Honest, Quality Hip Hop|first=Brandon|last=Goldner|date=July 14, 2016|work=BlazersEdge.com|access-date=October 6, 2020}} and his first EP on August 12, 2016, entitled ''Emerald District'',{{cite web|url=https://www.portlandmercury.com/music/2016/08/10/18465606/sneaker-wave|title=Sneaker Wave|first=Jenni|last=Moore|date=August 10, 2016|work=PortlandMercury.com|access-date=October 6, 2020}} which was produced by [[Seattle]] hip hop producer [[Jake One]]. ==References== {{reflist|30em}} ==External links== *{{Basketballstats|nba=101110|bbr=w/webstma02}} {{2005 NBA draft}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Webster, Martell}} [[Category:1986 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century African-American sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Seattle]] [[Category:Fort Worth Flyers players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:NBA high school draftees]] [[Category:Parade High School All-Americans (boys' basketball)]] [[Category:Portland Trail Blazers draft picks]] [[Category:Portland Trail Blazers players]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Small forwards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Edmonds, Washington]] [[Category:Washington Wizards players]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:Gary Ridgway]]
